title: Transit service can operate at national scale without proving equal usable mobility
source_unit: Federal Transit Administration National Transit Database 2024 annual products and national summary
geography: United States public transportation agencies and urbanized areas

denominator.unit: FTA National Transit Database agency reports and national operating summary

observations.method: FTA aggregation of National Transit Database agency reports for service, ridership, assets, funding, safety, and workforce; operating supply and passenger-use measures remain distinct.
observations.uncertainty: National totals combine modes, agencies, reporting types, and trip definitions; increases do not identify unique riders, essential trips, local reliability, fare burden, or household outcomes.
observations.subgroup: Nearly 3,000 public transit agencies, 18 modes, 502 urbanized areas, and reported national workforce and fleet.
observations.counterinterpretation: Higher trips and miles can reflect post-pandemic recovery, population/place composition, service changes, or concentrated use rather than equal access or improved welfare; a large system can still leave some trips unreachable.

related_sources.claim: FTA's 2024 national summary reports passenger trips, passenger miles, urbanized areas, workforce, and fleet context.
FTA documents the NTD service-data files and reconciliation boundaries for vehicle revenue miles and vehicles operated in maximum service.

boundary: This record measures national agency-reported transit operating scale and passenger use. It does not establish equal local access, fare affordability, reliability, safety, completed essential trips, household welfare, or political response.
